item.title: Affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequalities and optimal star bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.30689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish an affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequality by replacing the Euclidean fractional Orlicz seminorm with an energy obtained by minimizing over origin-symmetric star bodies of prescribed volume. Under finite lower and upper power growth assumptions, a subcritical upper growth bound, and a monotonicity condition on $t^{n/s+2}\Phi''(t)$, the resulting inequality has the same best constant as its Euclidean counterpart. The power case recovers the affine fractional Sobolev inequality of Haddad and Ludwig with the corresponding Luxemburg normalization. To establish this inequality, we investigate the underlying geometric extremal problem. For every nonzero smooth function of compact support, the existence and uniqueness of an optimal star body are proved under the growth assumptions alone, and its radial function is characterized by an equation involving $\Phi(t)+(s/n)t\Phi'(t)$. We also establish an anisotropic rearrangement inequality, together with its equality conditions under additional strictness assumptions. Moreover, the normalized local limit is investigated. The optimized energies converge to the local energy, and the radial functions of the minimizing bodies converge uniformly on the sphere. The limiting modular is determined by $\overline\Phi(t)=\int_0^t\Phi(\tau)\,d\tau/\tau$. Finally, we compare optimization over star bodies with optimization in the affine orbit.
item.dc:creator: Ai-Jun Li, Qingzhong Huang

item.title: Dual medial axes in finite-dimensional normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.30878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study medial axes of nonempty closed sets in finite-dimensional real normed spaces whose norms are $C^1$ away from the origin. Using the differential of the norm, we define the dual $k$-medial axis by requiring the contact covectors associated with nearest points to have affine dimension at least $k-1$. In dimension $n$, we prove that this set is $(n-k+1)$-rectifiable for every $1\le k\le n+1$, and hence has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-k+1$. We give a direct geometric proof and characterize the dual medial axes through the superdifferential of the squared distance function, obtaining an alternative proof from a theorem of Alberti, Ambrosio, and Cannarsa on singularities of semiconvex functions. Under the additional assumption of strict convexity, the ordinary and dual medial axes coincide for $k=2,3$, yielding the corresponding rectifiability results for ordinary medial axes. For $k=4$, however, the ordinary rectifiability conclusion can fail even for norms arbitrarily close to Euclidean: we construct norms on $\mathbb R^3$ with smooth positively curved unit spheres arbitrarily $C^\infty$-close to the Euclidean sphere, together with four-point sets whose ordinary $4$-medial axes contain nondegenerate line segments.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Durand, Xiangyu Liang, Sicheng Zhang

item.title: Lipschitz clustering in normed spaces and barycentric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every normed space $X$ and integers $1\le k<n$, we construct a Lipschitz retraction from $X(n)$ onto $X(k)$ with constant at most $2+8n(n-1)$, independently of the dimension of $X$. Here $X(n)$ consists of the nonempty subsets of $X$ with at most $n$ points, equipped with the Hausdorff metric. For the consecutive case $k=n-1$, a separate construction gives the sharper asymptotic bound $O(n\log n)$. These results extend to barycentric metric spaces and settle some open problems on Lipschitz retractions.
item.dc:creator: Leonid V. Kovalev

item.title: An algebraic proof of 1-extension
item.description: arXiv:2610.31212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new proof that 1-extension preserves generic local rigidity of bar-joint frameworks in all dimensions. The proof does not use a special position argument, which makes the approach potentially useful for X-replacement in 3-space. Instead, the balancing conditions recently introduced by the first author use directed paths in the line graph, and by modifying the end of these paths, we transfer a self-stress on the 1-extended graph back to the original. Treating the new vertex as variable allows us to extract the balancing condition of the smaller graph as one coefficient of a homogeneous quadratic. A Lean 4 formalization of the main results accompanies the paper.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Heaton, Martin Winter

item.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < \pi/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $\pi/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Larotonda

item.title: On isoperimetric local-Bollob\'as-Thomason inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2601.15044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the following isoperimetric-type inequality: for every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and some $\sigma\subset[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there exists a suitable Hanner polytope $B_K$ with the same volume as $K$ and such that the volume of each of its orthogonal projections onto every subspace whose basis is formed by the canonical vectors $\{e_i:i\in\tau\cup([n]\setminus\sigma)\}$, for every $\tau\subseteq\sigma$, bounds from below the volume of the corresponding projections of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno

item.title: On the Geometry of Wasserstein Barycenter II: Riemannian Rigidity, Essential Non-Branching, and Finsler Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.19564v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wasserstein barycenters provide a notion of weighted mean for probability measures on a metric space. We prove that the barycenter curvature-dimension condition ${\rm BCD}(K,N)$ is equivalent to ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ for $K\in \mathbb R$ and $1<N<\infty$. This gives a new characterization of Riemannian curvature-dimension spaces by entropy inequalities at barycenters of finite families of measures. As a byproduct, we introduce an almost ${\rm BCD}$ condition that allows an additive error in the entropy inequality. It is stable under measured Gromov-Hausdorff convergence and implies essential non-branching when the error is sufficiently small. The resulting class contains non-Riemannian Finsler spaces. Within the ${\rm BCD}$ framework, this answers an open problem posed by Ambrosio in his 2018 ICM survey. We further bound the failure of the parallelogram identity for cotangent norms in terms of the entropy error.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Deng-Yu Liu

item.title: On Densities in the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer Distance Problems over the Integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.10665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the classical Erd\H{o}s and Falconer distance problems and Magyar's work on distance sets in $\mathbb Z^d$, we study discrete analogues of the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer unpinned and pinned distance problems over the integers. We ask how the discrete Hausdorff dimension of a set $A\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ influences the size of its squared-distance sets, measured by generalized upper natural density and upper discrete mass dimension. We propose conjectures for both problems and prove the unpinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2,3$ and the pinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2$. For the unpinned problem in higher dimensions, we obtain explicit lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets using elementary integer sphere counting, results on the Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem, and $\ell^p$-improving inequalities for discrete spherical averages. For the pinned problem, we obtain lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets for some or every pin. We also establish more general results involving upper discrete mass dimension, upper discrete Banach dimension, and affine dimension, including bounds on the affine dimension of the exceptional set of pins. We construct examples showing that both conjectures are sharp in low dimensions. Further examples demonstrate how the distinctions among discrete Hausdorff dimension, upper discrete mass dimension, and upper discrete Banach dimension lead to different phenomena in the unpinned and pinned distance problems, including limitations on the nontrivial upper bounds these dimensions can provide for the dimensions of distance sets.
item.dc:creator: Eyvindur Ari Palsson, Jian-An Wang

item.title: An Intersection Product for the Polytope Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2504.16678v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new multiplication for the polytope algebra, defined via the intersection of polytopes. After establishing the foundational properties of this intersection product, we investigate finite-dimensional subalgebras that arise naturally from this construction. These subalgebras can be regarded as volumetric analogues of the graded M\"obius algebra, which appears in the context of the Dowling--Wilson conjecture. We conjecture that they also satisfy the injective hard Lefschetz property and the Hodge--Riemann relations, and we prove these in degree one.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Wannerer

item.title: Translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2601.14193v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a series of papers, Weil initiated the investigation of translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies, which include as prime examples Federer's curvature measures. In this paper, we continue this line of research by introducing new tools to study curvature measures. Our main results suggest that the space of curvature measures, which is graded by degree and parity, is highly structured: We conjecture that each graded component has length at most $2$ as a representation of the general linear group, and we prove this in degrees $0$ and $n-2$. Beyond this conjectural picture, our methods yield a characterization of Federer's curvature measures under weaker assumptions.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Adv. Math. 503 (2026), part C, Paper No. 111275
item.dc:creator: Jakob Schuhmacher, Thomas Wannerer

item.title: A Recognizable Substitution for the Anti-Penrose Tiling
item.description: arXiv:2603.15549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a substitution on six marked rhombs, called Seabed, with inflation factor $\varphi^3$. We prove that its tiling space is mutually locally derivable with the unmarked Anti-Penrose pentagrid hull. Eleven vertex patches of depth at most four recognize the parent vertices: their acceptance domains coincide with the five internally contracted windows. Matching the fine tiles around each parent rhomb to a replacement patch recovers their markings uniquely. The inverse local maps have a uniform finite radius and extend to all singular limit tilings in the hull. The construction also gives a recognizable parent hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Miki Imura

item.title: Weak rank rigidity for groups with a navigable path system
item.description: arXiv:2605.29837v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that groups with a mild form of non-positive curvature (a navigable path system) satisfy the weak rank rigidity conjecture: they either have linear divergence or a Morse element. This class includes discrete groups of projective automorphisms of open convex cones, Helly groups (answering a question of Genevois), Coxeter groups, weak Garside groups (in particular Deligne's groups and fundamental groups of Salvetti complexes of oriented matroids), hierarchically hyperbolic groups, and other examples. Along the way, we show that those groups satisfy the Morse local-to-global property, providing a unified proof for the whole class. In the metric setting, the same condition of non-positive curvature allows to provide a local definition (that is, in a sense, optimal) of rank one/Morse geodesics, mirroring the one using parallel Jacobi fields from Riemannian geometry; to deduce linearity of divergence from linearity on a sequence; to obtain new cases in which Morse geodesics are strongly contracting. The main new tool introduced is the generalised contraction space, a hyperbolic space that encodes the negative curvature of a given space.
item.dc:creator: Cornelia Drutu, Davide Spriano, Stefanie Zbinden

item.title: Approximation algorithm for mixed volumes of a constant number of convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.08248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the computation of mixed volumes of convex sets given as rational subspace sections of bodies described by membership oracles. The sets need not have nonempty interior. For positive multiplicities $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k=n$, we give a randomized algorithm that computes a relative $\varepsilon$-approximation with probability at least $1-\delta$. Its running time is polynomial in Gurvits' factor $\Gamma_\alpha=(n^n/n!)\prod_i\alpha_i!/\alpha_i^{\alpha_i}$, the input presentation length, and $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and linear in $1+\log\delta^{-1}$, with degree independent of $k$. The running-time bound holds for every choice of the random bits, and zero mixed volumes are detected exactly. We extend the capacity-scaling and sampling method of Narayanan--Roy by using rational projections and a smooth mixed Monge--Amp\`ere representation. In particular, the algorithm runs in randomized polynomial time when the number of distinct convex sets is bounded above by a constant.
item.dc:creator: Hariharan Narayanan

item.title: Positive-measure intersections of Bedford-McMullen carpets under similitudes
item.description: arXiv:2610.09277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K=K(n,m,\Gamma)$ be a Bedford-McMullen carpet with $n>m\geq2$ and $1<\#\Gamma<nm$, and let $\mu$ be a self-affine measure on $K$ with strictly positive weights. We prove that every similitude $f(z)=rOz+a$ satisfying $\mu(K\cap f(K))>0$ has a diagonal or anti-diagonal orthogonal part $O$, without any arithmetic restrictions on the defining bases. Under the same intersection hypothesis, we also show that $r\in n^{\mathbb{Q}}\cup m^{\mathbb{Q}}$ whenever $K$ is not a segment. For isometries satisfying this hypothesis, we further prove that $f(K)$ is simply a translate of $K$, thereby establishing a strengthened form of the 2010 conjecture of Elekes, Keleti and M\'ath\'e in this planar self-affine context.
item.dc:creator: Ding-Kun Hu, Huo-Jun Ruan, Jian-Ci Xiao
